facts.text: Director Steven LaMorte grew up on Staten Island, so a slasher set on its famous ferry is a hometown project for him.
The ferry used for filming is a decommissioned Staten Island Ferry that Saturday Night Live stars Colin Jost and Pete Davidson bought in 2022.
Steamboat Willie entered the public domain on January 1, 2024. The Screamboat project was announced the very next day.
While scouting, director Steven LaMorte and star/producer Amy Schumacher reportedly rode the Staten Island Ferry 15 to 20 times in a single day.
Director Steven LaMorte says the princess-costumed party girls came from a real group he saw on the Staten Island Ferry every Saturday night in his twenties.
The birthday girls are Disney princesses in disguise: Cindi (Cinderella), Ariana (Ariel), Jazzy (Jasmine), Bella (Belle) and Rory (Aurora).
The ferry's name, Mortimer, was an early suggestion for what Walt Disney would call Mickey Mouse, before Walt's wife Lillian pushed for Mickey.
Amber, the paramedic played by producer Amy Schumacher, is named after Princess Amber from Disney's kids' series Sofia the First.
Deckhand Pete is named after Pegleg Pete, the cat villain who captained the boat in the original 1928 Steamboat Willie cartoon.
Fans guessed Selena, the aspiring designer played by Allison Pittel, was based on YouTuber Jenny Nicholson. Director Steven LaMorte flatly denied it.
Director Steven LaMorte previously made The Mean One (2022), a horror parody of the Grinch, another famous character turned slasher.
Producer Amy Schumacher says the team consulted a lawyer before shooting. Willie must always wear his hat: without it he'd read as post-1928 Mickey Mouse, who is still under copyright.
Willie actor David Howard Thornton is on the autism spectrum and used to be an elementary school teacher before becoming a horror star.
Willie is played by David Howard Thornton, best known as the silent, mime-like killer Art the Clown in the Terrifier films.
The mouse puppet and costume were designed by Quantum Creation FX, which helped keep Willie's kills practical.
Getting David Howard Thornton into Willie's makeup and fur suit took about three to four hours every shooting day, per director Steven LaMorte and producer Amy Schumacher.
TMZ reported the shoot used so much fake blood on the borrowed ferry that a special cleaning crew had to be hired.
Halfway through day one, David Howard Thornton found a breathing technique inside the mask that made Willie's whiskers move. The crew hadn't planned it, says producer Amy Schumacher.
Jesse Kove, who plays NYPD Lieutenant Diaz, is best known as David on the Netflix series Cobra Kai.
Willie actor David Howard Thornton's first stage role as a kid was Mickey Mouse. Director Steven LaMorte says Thornton still does the voice in public, even when asked not to.
Dialogue is stuffed with Disney song titles. A party girl promising 'a whole new world' is a nod to Aladdin.
Another Disney song nod: a crew member says 'be our guest' and calls the lower deck a grand ballroom, echoing Beauty and the Beast.
Brian Quinn (Mitch McEverly) of Impractical Jokers served eight years as a real New York City firefighter with the FDNY.
One Willie kill can take a crowd: an actor on each hand, a puppeteer on the mouse, someone twisting the torso, and David Howard Thornton about 30 feet back, says director Steven LaMorte.
Tyler Posey, the Teen Wolf star who plays Radio Operator Mike, was once considered for the role of Jacob Black in Twilight (2008).
Michael Leavy, who plays Deckhand Bert Brunswick, also co-produced the film, and he appeared in Terrifier and Terrifier 2 alongside Willie actor David Howard Thornton.
'Can you feel the love tonight?' is another Disney song title slipped into the script, this one from The Lion King.
David Howard Thornton stands roughly 6'5" in the Willie suit, so props he holds had to be built oversized to keep the pint-sized mouse illusion working.
The 'pizza rat' joke nods to a viral New York subway video of a rat dragging a slice of pizza. 'Rizzo the rat' is the Muppets' rodent.
Even docked, the real ferry shook whenever big freighters passed, and shots on the moving ferry couldn't be locked off, the filmmakers told PopHorror.
Screamboat cost about $2 million to make and grossed only around $393,000 in its limited theatrical run.
The team decided early in scripting that Willie would be tiny, inspired by the 'Partners' statue of Walt Disney holding hands with Mickey Mouse.
In Barry's story, the scientist experimenting on Willie is the Mad Doctor from a 1933 Mickey cartoon, and a sketch of Oswald the Lucky Rabbit is visible.
A planned cameo reference to the first Mouseketeer was dropped because, director Steven LaMorte says, the lawyers 'wouldn't clear it because she's a real person.'
A tattooed fan at a horror convention told director Steven LaMorte he'd spotted the film's hidden Mary Poppins reference. LaMorte's reply: 'Mission accomplished!'
Screamboat was shot on RED cinema cameras, and the production's data cards and drives were supplied by storage maker OWC.
Willie never speaks. David Howard Thornton developed his giggles and whistles himself in costume, after co-writer Matthew Garcia-Dunn suggested whistling as his way to communicate.
Screamboat was first set for release on January 24, 2025. It instead premiered April 1, 2025 at the Regal Union Square in Manhattan before a limited release April 2.
Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes lists 51% positive from 35 critics, and Metacritic gives it 44 out of 100.
A sequel, Screamboat 2: Nothing Stays Dead, has been announced as in development.
Director Steven LaMorte told Gizmodo he got into filmmaking 'as a backdoor way to be an Imagineer.' He calls the Disney nods 'vital to the DNA of the flick,' not just Easter eggs.
Variety's Peter Debruge found it fun for 'desecrating powerful brands, like Disney.' RogerEbert.com's Brian Tallerico gave it two stars out of four.
The film's gore logic, per director Steven LaMorte: Willie thinks he's still a cartoon and doesn't realize people bleed, so the kills were made over-the-top to be funny.
In the end credits, crew member Sean Kenney is credited as a 'lense technician,' a misspelling of 'lens.'
